name: Sunshine, last full day (satellite)
summary: Sunshine energy that reached the ground in each city over the last full day, added up from satellite hours, and how much the clouds took away. Not what a panel makes.

el.name: Ήλιος, τελευταία πλήρης μέρα (δορυφόρος)
el.summary: Η ενέργεια του ήλιου που έφτασε στο έδαφος σε κάθε πόλη την τελευταία πλήρη μέρα, αθροισμένη από ώρες δορυφόρου, και πόσο την έκοψαν τα σύννεφα. Όχι η παραγωγή ενός πάνελ.

licence.attribution: Satellite radiation data by Open-Meteo.com (DWD, EUMETSAT MTG)

restrictions: Free API is for non-commercial use only (educational use counts; ads or subscriptions do not)

coverage.area: Europe and Africa (the view of the MTG satellite)

update.note: A day counts only when every hour of daylight has a value; we add up the hours ourselves.

variables.note: hourly satellite values added up over one day (kWh per m2)
that day's sunshine divided by what a cloud-free sky would give

quality.uncertainty: Added up from estimates, not measured by an instrument at the school. Errors in single hours partly cancel over a day but never vanish.
known_issues: One pixel about 2.5 km wide, not the school roof
The share of cloud-free sunshine is a clue about cloudiness, not a measurement of cloud cover
1 kWh/m2 is one hour of very strong sun. It is sunlight, not electricity: panel output also depends on size, angle, dirt, heat and efficiency
School light sensors report lux, not kWh/m2 or W/m2: the quantities are different and are never compared

upstream.name: DWD surface solar radiation from the EUMETSAT MTG imager

use_for: How sunny the last full day was in a city
Context for a talk about school solar panels
not_for: Saying how much electricity a solar panel makes
Comparing with the classroom light sensors: lux and kWh/m2 are different things
Saying how much cloud there was

notes: Same service and same upstream as openmeteo-satellite-solar, so the brain counts them as one. The clear-sky column exists only for the DWD product; if the service refuses it or leaves it empty, only the energy is shown. The service could not be called from the build sandbox: after the deploy look in the Railway log for the line 'first answer'.
